root_cause: The datepicker component formats the input value as a locale string (e.g., MM/DD/YYYY) when there is no separate display element, but the form expects the ISO string (YYYY-MM-DD) for submission. This causes the submitted departure date to be in the wrong format when the user leaves the field without changing the date.
repair_strategy: Modify the `_formatDate` method to return the ISO string when the datepicker is attached to an input element and there is no separate display element, ensuring the input value remains in ISO format for proper form submission while preserving locale formatting for elements with a dedicated display element.
expected_accessibility_effect: The change ensures form data is submitted in the correct ISO format, which is machine-readable and consistent. The date display in input fields will now show ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD) instead of locale format, which remains accessible and unambiguous though may be less familiar to some users.
functional_risks: Users accustomed to local date formats may find ISO format less readable
If the form relies on locale format for display (e.g., readability), user experience may be impacted
Form submission will now work correctly with ISO format
verification_requirements: Verify departure date field retains ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD) after initialization and after interacting with datepicker without changing date
Verify selecting a date updates input value to corresponding ISO string
Verify form submission includes departure date in ISO format
Ensure change does not break datepicker functionality for elements with separate display element (non-inputs or when displayElement is configured)
